disprovenClaims: CLAIM (the phase's own, § 3.2): 'OnClientConnected reads the ticket's team — it already has the verified ticket, since it verifies it to accept the connection at all'. DISPROVEN by reading the type: ConnectionInfo carries ConnectionId, RemoteAddress, SmoothedRttMs, State, PlayerId, Stats and DisplayName — no ticket. The verification happens in UdpTransportServer at the handshake, and the tick loop sees only what that parse chose to keep. Acting on the phase's wording would have produced a compile error at best; taking 'it already has it' as licence to re-parse would have re-read attacker-controlled bytes in a layer with no secret to check them with. The team rides ConnectionInfo, exactly as ledger X-36 carried the display name.

CLAIM (the phase's own, § 3.3): adding ConnectDenyReason.TeamFull = 7 is enough for 'a join onto a full side is refused with TeamFull'. DISPROVEN by following the failing path: it calls Transport.Disconnect(connectionId, DisconnectReason.ServerFull), a DisconnectReason, because the slot claim runs AFTER the handshake completes. Code 7 has no sender on that path and could never reach a player. DisconnectReason.TeamFull = 9 was added alongside it; without it the criterion-6 evidence would have been a value in an enum and a screenshot nobody could take.

CLAIM (the phase's own, § 1.1 + criterion 5): the three-join, middle-disconnect sequence 'leaves two players on team 0' under the defect and one per side under the fix. DISPROVEN by exhaustive simulation of both strategies against the lobby's own balancer — 2-8 joins x every departure slot x 0-3 further joins — which found ZERO single-departure sequences that end with different live teams. That sequence leaves 2v0 under the FIX as well, and § 6 of the same phase puts the only remedy (moving a player already in the match) out of scope. Escalated to the owner rather than fudged; criterion 5 was reworded to a two-departure sequence that genuinely reds on the old code.

CLAIM: 'the team round-trip tests prove the layout'. DISPROVEN by mutation: swapping OffsetTeam and OffsetDisplayName leaves 288 of 290 tests green, INCLUDING every team round-trip, because both halves of a round trip move together. Only the hex sample reds. This is why freeze-gate condition 2 asks for a hex sample.

CLAIM: 'parsing the team proves it reaches the server'. DISPROVEN by mutation: deleting connection.Team = ticketTeam leaves every parser test green and reds one wiring test. This is the exact trap the display name fell into for four phases (X-36), one field over.
reachableRegressions: A v5 client against a v6 server: every byte from offset 16 moved, so a v5 ticket's first name byte 'N' (0x4E) is read as team 78, and the join is refused for a side that does not exist. MITIGATED as intended — PROTOCOL_VERSION moved in the code AND in the spec's fenced block AND in the prose header, so the handshake answers CONNECT_DENIED code 2 before a ticket is ever parsed. The client and server ship together; this is the designed outcome of a wire change, not an escape.

A name whose 15th byte is mid-sequence rendering as U+FFFD in every killfeed line for a whole match. MITIGATED by the existing back-off loop, which was correct for 16 and is correct for 15 — but was UNTESTED at any boundary until now. Mutation 2 confirms the new tests see it.

S_PLAYER_LIST still declares MaxNameBytes = 16 while a ticket now delivers at most 15. NOT a break: the field is a bound, not a fixed width, and a 15-byte name fits it. Recorded because the two numbers now differ on purpose and a future reader will ask.

IRONFRONT_CLIENT_TEAM defaults to 0, so any existing scripted multi-client run that does not set it now puts every client on team 0 — and, once a side fills, is refused. run-lane-b.ps1's roster was given explicit alternating teams for exactly this reason; any other runner in the repository that mints its own tickets needs the same treatment. The load harness alternates by clientIndex.
missingProof: Criterion 6's literal screenshot. The refusal is proven from BOTH sides at runtime (server log and client log) in two controlled runs, and the two sentences are pinned by a test — but no image was captured: a refused lane-B client renders no frame, and LobbyShellOverlay, which draws MasterSession.LastError in red, is on the master-server shell flow rather than the standalone path lane-B uses.

Criterion 7 against a genuinely old BINARY. Tested against undefined codes 8, 9 and 255 on today's build, which exercises the same default arm a v5 build would take for code 7. No v5 binary was rebuilt to be shot at.

ServerTickLoop's ServerFull arm. The contrast run's third client was refused BY THE TRANSPORT at capacity and never reached OnClientConnected — no conn 3 line in that server log. The player-facing contrast is real and proven; that particular branch is not what proved it.
